rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 - own field experiment at Chott Meriem, Tunisia, April-June 2011, cucumber under surface drip (T0) and SDI at 15 cm (T1) and 30 cm (T2), with TDR soil moisture, leaf area, yield and WUE measurements. Q2: Section 3.5 / Fig. 8 and Abstract - highest WUE recorded in T2 (15 kg m-3), about 20% and 13% higher than T1 and T0, with the same water applied to all treatments; Section 3.1 / Figs 3-4 - soil water stock 10.2% greater under T1 than surface drip, interpreted as weaker evaporative losses under SDI. Q4: Section 2.2 and Section 3.1-3.2 / Figs 3-5 - daily TDR measurement of soil water stock to 60 cm under each dripline depth, used to infer lower evaporation and water losses under SDI (the intermediate variable linking SDI to WUE).
rows.notes: WUE difference between treatments was reported as not statistically significant (Section 3.5). Deep seepage and soil evaporation were not measured directly; drainage losses for T2 and reduced evaporation for T1 are inferred from the soil water stock measurements, so Q4 is a yes with that caveat. Q3: WUE derived from yield and applied water, and soil water stock from TDR (gravimetric sampling used only to calibrate TDR) - one method per variable, no triangulation of the WUE result. Q5/Q6: single site, single crop, single season, 212 m2 plot. Q7: statement that 30 cm depth was 'probably acceptable on our soil type and climate when the crop is fully irrigated' is a scoping/hedged remark, not stated as a requirement; the 'proper depth' condition is cited from Camp (1998). Q8: only 'further observations are needed'; the remark that soil water content is an imperfect indicator of plant water status is general discussion rather than a stated limitation of their own result. Q9: only SNK letter groupings and means; no SD, SE, CI or range reported.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 - own field experiment on cucumber under surface drip and SDI at 15 and 30 cm in Tunisia, 2011.
rows.notes: The study does not measure, observe or mention weeds or any pest at all. It reports only soil water stock, soil water stock variation, leaf area, yield and WUE under different dripline depths. No own evidence on weed suppression by SDI.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Figures are referenced but not reproduced in the text, so any error bars in Figs 4, 6-8 cannot be verified; only SNK letter groupings are described. Single-season, single-site field trial on a 212 m2 plot with surface drip and two SDI depths.
